title: Biases in the Blind Spot: Detecting What LLMs Fail to Mention

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual input variation by modifying gender-identifying information such as pronouns, first names, and explicit gender markers in resumes and applications while leaving other content unchanged.
Counterfactual substitution using names stereotypically associated with specific racial groups (e.g., Black-sounding vs. White-sounding names) and explicit mentions of racial or ethnic identity.
Modifying input text to alter writing formality, inject grammatical errors to test English proficiency bias, or explicitly add language skills (e.g., Spanish fluency) to observe decision shifts.
Injecting explicit statements about religious affiliation (e.g., attending a church or temple) or using name-based religious cues to compare approval rates across different religions.

Instructing the model to impersonate political identities (Democrat or Republican) via system prompts, with and without concealment instructions, to measure shifts in agreement on Political Compass propositions.
Name-based counterfactual substitutions associated with specific cultural or regional backgrounds (e.g., Latin American vs. Indian) evaluated in multilingual contexts.
